explanation_excerpt: You can run kbd-reflect any time you want a snapshot of how the phase is going so far — it's a good habit to reflect partway through a long phase, even with several changes still pendi

gaps.description: Claims the closing/reflection stage can be run at any time, including partway through a phase with changes still pending. The stage requires ALL changes to have status DONE, and the stage gate rejects early execution.
gaps.corpus_ref: MISCONCEPTION: /kbd-reflect can run before all changes are DONE

gaps.description: The closing stage is gated on completion, not usable as a mid-phase 'snapshot' or check-in tool.

Omits what the closing stage actually produces: a reflection document with per-goal MET/PARTIAL/NOT MET status, technical debt notes, lessons learned, a recommended next phase, and passage through the sycophancy-correction reflector gate.

transfer_problems: A phase has 8 planned changes; progress.json shows 5 marked DONE and 3 still PROPOSED. The operator runs the closing/reflection stage anyway. What happens, and why?

After the closing stage successfully produces a reflection document, what three categories of information must the report include about each phase goal, and what mechanism checks the reflection itself before it is logged?
